recipes.name: No Bake Lemon-Lime Chiffon Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 ounce) package lime flavored Jell-O® mix
1 (12 fluid ounce) can evaporated milk, chilled

steps.text: Pour the boiling water into a small bowl, and stir in the gelatin until dissolved. Set aside.
Beat the evaporated milk in a mixer bowl until stiff. Add the lemon juice and sugar; continue beating. Stir in the gelatin mixture and blend thoroughly. Chill for 1 hour.
Pour filling into the crusts. Chill until firm, about 1 hour, or overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: No Bake Lemon-Lime Chiffon Pie
raw_recipe.description: Fresh lemon juice, lime gelatin, and evaporated milk create a light, airy filling in this easy, no-bake chilled pie with a graham cracker crust. A nice bonus: The recipe makes two pies for the effort of one.

review.reviewBody:
I have looked for this recipe in the past, but could not remember the name of it until now. Growing up, my best friend's mom made this often for us.
It is delicious and easy! She used all different flavors of gelatin. I remember that strawberry and orange were especially good. Yum !!...can't wait to make this !!!

Absolutely great recipe for someone looking for a delicious light dessert with few calories. Only needs a third of a cup of sugar though and I used sugar free lemon jello. You can even leave out the crust and eat it as a whipped pudding with a dash of canned whipped cream.

This has been my favorite pie for decades. I'd never seen a recipe for it anywhere except my mom's old recipe box.

There are two significant differences with how Mom made it, though. First, we only use 1/3 of a cup of sugar. I can't imagine a whole cup. Second, we always used a chocolate crust. The Oreo crusts are what I use now.

This is a great recipe. I cut the amount of sugar to 1/2 cup and didn't miss it at all. In fact, next time I make this, I will only use 1/4 of a cup because it was still quite sweet. I also added a bit of cinnamon and ginger to the crust for a little flavour. So easy and definately a crowd pleaser.

Yum, delicious and easy. Following the advice of the previous review, I also used half the sugar, and the sweetness was just right. I opted to use fresh lime juice (the juice of one lime). I didn't know you could beat evaporated milk stiff, so it was a new experience for me. I'm going to make this recipe for my daughter's class when she shares the book "Pickle Chiffon Pie". Thanks, Patti!

We called this 'green pie' in our household. My mom made it on special occasions, not because the recipe is complicated, but because my brother and I would literally fight over what was left. My mom finally started making us each an extra bowl of filling. Peace came to the house (until the next reason to fight lol). I think the secret of a good green pie is in the frothing of the mixture. My mom also added the zest from 2 lemons and the juices.

This recipe was very simple to follow and make. Be sure to thoroughly stir up the mixture before pouring into the crust!

Also, I didn't have like jello mix but I did have lemon. Easy fix; swap them around!
I agree with others to reduce the sugar
Very easy, made 1/2 though for 1 pie. Will make for family reunion.
I added a bit of cinnamon and ginger to the crust for a little flavour. So easy and definately a crowd pleaser. Thank You!

I wasn't blown away by this pie. I've been looking for a recipe similar to this, and haven't had any luck locating. I followed the directions exactly, and it was too much sugar. The texture of the filling was a bit foamy. Overall, it was good and light. I did receive compliments. However, this is not something I'll make again.
My family LOVED this pie. It was very light and refreshing. I will definitey make it again.
Well this was'nt my favorite but okay. I was in a little rush and I probably should have beat the evaporated milk little better because it was a little too creamy. But the taste was okay anyway.
This was okay. A little too tart and texture was on the foamy side... but it was definitely edible.
